# dsh-browser
A browser panel for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI. It is a Cordis bundle: a Host half that adds fenced
HTTP routes and one agent tool, and a web Client half that registers a `browser` main panel plus a
es and one agent tool, and a web Client half that registers a `browser` main panel plus a rail icon.
中文说明见 README.zh.md.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package declares `dsh.bundle` (`cordis.patch.yml` inserts one Host row) and `dsh.client` (the we
b half). There is no build step and no runtime dependency: the Client bundle is plain JavaScript loa
ded through `window.__ModuleLoader__`.
After installing, the rail icon (a globe, after *Plugins* and *Schedules*) opens the panel.
**Host-side edits need a row reload** — disable and re-enable the plugin row, or restart the Harness
: the Loader keeps the imported ES module. Client edits reload through HMR.
## What it does
### Tabs and the omnibox
- Back / forward / reload / home, a tab strip, and an omnibox that treats input as a URL, a workspac

e file path, or a search query.
- `Ctrl`/`⌘`-click, middle-click and `Alt`+`Enter` open a new tab (S

hift keeps it in the foreground). The same intent is reported from inside rendered pages.
- Browser
state — profiles, tabs, bookmarks, history, extension switches, download records — is stored in this
origin's `localStorage` under `dsh-browser.state.v1`.
### Search
The omnibox calls `POST /dshbrowse/api/search`, which runs `ctx.web.search` through the Harness web
seam (the configured provider, `deepseek-official`, uses the native `web_search` server tool). The p
anel renders the returned `sources[]` natively and can export the list as CSV or JSON. Results are c
ached per query for the session, so the same search does not cost a second model call.
### Browsing profiles bound to folders
Each profile owns its own tabs, bookmarks, history and extension switches. Binding a folder to a pro
file also registers it as a Harness workspace (`workspaces.create({ path })`), after which:

- **New Agent session** opens a session in that folder;
- the page action **Send to Agent** drafts a
prompt from the page title, description and headings into a session in that workspace, then switche
s to the conversation.
### Page rendering
Two views share one tab:
| View | How |
| **Page** (default) | `GET /dshbrowse/api/render?url=…` fetches the page with `ctx.web.fetch`, inje
cts a `<base>` pointing at the real site so its CSS, images and fonts resolve, strips the site's scr
ipts and its `meta` CSP / refresh, appends a navigation bridge, and returns the document from the pa
nel's own origin. The frame is `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-downloads allow-modals"` — no `allow-sa

me-origin`, so the document keeps an opaque origin. |
| **Reader** | `GET /dshbrowse/api/page` retur
ns the same fetch verbatim; the client parses it with `DOMParser` into a document model (h1–h6, p, l
i, pre, img, table, links) that extensions can rewrite. |
Because the framed document is served from the panel origin, a site's `X-Frame-Options` / `frame-anc
estors` no longer applies. The trade-off is that site JavaScript is stripped: a client-rendered SPA
may need Reader instead.
### Workspace files
Files the Harness writes into a workspace can be opened directly:
- `GET /dshbrowse/api/files?dir=…` lists one directory; `GET /dshbrowse/api/file?path=…` serves one
file. HTML/CSS are rewritten so a generated report keeps its stylesheet, images and scripts; everyth

ing else is streamed with the right content type and `no-cache`.
- Root paths only: a canonical path

outside every registered workspace directory (and the downloads folder) is refused with 403.
- HTML
, SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP, PDF, Markdown, plain text, JSON/CSV, video and audio are rendered inline; the n

ew-tab page and a dedicated file browser list them.
- `POST /dshbrowse/api/inbox` consumers: the `br
owser_open` tool queues a URL or a workspace file and the panel opens it in a tab.
### Extensions
A Chrome-style, declarative extension system:
| Field | Meaning |

| `permissions` | shown in the manager, informational |
| `contentScripts[].matches` | `*`, `*://hos

t/*` patterns decide where a script applies |
| `contentScripts[].hide` | CSS selectors removed befo

re the document model is built |
| `contentScripts[].highlight(s)` | words marked in the reader |
|

`contentScripts[].width` | reader width |
| `action` | gives the extension a toolbar button and a pa

entScripts[].width` | reader width |
| `action` | gives the extension a toolbar button and a panel |
Extensions cannot execute code. Built in: ad/tracker cleanup, keyword highlighting, focus reading (p
aragraph limit), page outline. The manager installs from a pasted `manifest.json`, enables/disables,
removes, and offers three suggested manifests.
### Downloads
Everything is written to a real folder, never overwritten (`note (1).txt`):
| Entry point | Product |
| Page → download | page HTML (relative references rewritten to absolute URLs), article Markdown, ar

ticle plain text |
| File page → download | the workspace file; a copied HTML page has its relative

references rewritten to `file:///` paths so it still renders |
| Search results | CSV or JSON of the

source list |
[该节后续省略]
## Security model

- Every route is refused unless the request passes `ctx.connection.requestRejection`.
- Path admissi
on: `realpath` the request, then require containment in a registered workspace directory or the down

loads folder; traversal and symlink escapes answer 403.
- Rendered and local pages run in a sandboxe
d frame without `allow-same-origin`, so their markup cannot reach the Harness API even though it is

served from the panel origin. Proxied pages additionally have their scripts stripped.
- Extension ma

nifests only contribute selectors, words and a width; there is no code execution path.
- Download fi
le names are sanitized and writes never overwrite.
## Compatibility
- Host services: `web`, `webServer`, `connection` (required), `tools` (optional — enables `browser_o

pen`).
- Client injections: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout` (declares `main` and `sidebar.panell

ist`), `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale`.
- No `dependencies`; the official `@deepseek-ai/*` packages
resolve from the installation.
